transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Starlake Channel Lead), Priya Sharma (VP Partnerships), Aisha Rao (Solutions Architect)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): Review of co-sell pipeline, prioritization of pilot accounts, technical requirements for a benchmark pilot (Horizon Health), and next steps around partner portal access and co-sell motions. Discussion touched on pricing, dedicated vs hosted, and SOC2/SAML requirements for two enterprise deals.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, uh, quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the pipeline.
[00:10] Liam O'Neill: Yeah hi, Liam here. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Priya Sharma: Priya on my end.
[00:14] Aisha Rao: Aisha hi.
[00:15] Ethan Brooks: Ethan from Redwood, thanks.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda 1) pipeline review and prioritization, 2) technical blockers and pilot plan for Horizon Health, 3) partner ops (portal, PR, co-sell leads), 4) next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Priya Sharma: Sounds good.
[00:30] Liam O'Neill: Yep.

[00:32] Maya Chen: Ok first up, high level, we pulled the list you shared last week about eight co-sell prospects. We highlighted three that look ready: Horizon Health (prod ML platform team), Meridian Logistics, and Beacon Retail. Liam, can you confirm those are the ones you're leaning in on?
[00:48] Liam O'Neill: Yeah that's right. Horizon's probably the closest, they've got an internal budget and a pilot RFP. Meridian is more procurement-y, maybe mid Q3. Beacon's exploratory.
[00:58] Ethan Brooks: When you say "pilot RFP" for Horizon, do you have any idea on their success criteria? e.g., latency SLA, cost targets, regional residency?
[01:05] Liam O'Neill: From the call notes, they're focused on latency under 300ms for user-facing completions and prefer a private deployment for PHI-ish data; they also asked about SOC 2 and SAML.
[01:15] Aisha Rao: Yeah, they mentioned HIPAA-ish constraints, so they'd like VPC or private. We heard Redwood Dedicated might fit, but cost is a concern.
[01:24] Maya Chen: Right. Dedicated is the simplest path to meet residency and isolation requirements; Redwood Private (VPC) is also on the table, we can scope an on-premish plan if needed. Cost-wise, we can show a few options: hosted with encryption+contract terms, dedicated reserved, or private. We'll include model/quantization tradeoffs to hit their cost targets.
[01:43] Priya Sharma: Any quick thoughts on where AWS Bedrock or Databricks would show up as blockers? Horizon asked about easy infra integration, and we've seen them favor providers with existing contracts.
[01:53] Ethan Brooks: From a technical standpoint, Databricks has a strong ML infra story, but our differentiator is production inference economics: continuous batching, KV cache, kernel selection — it can give them better per-token costs at scale. Bedrock is strong for managed models but less flexible for private/VPC variants.
[02:10] Liam O'Neill: Ok good to note, we'll arm the AE on Horizon with that value prop.

[02:20] Maya Chen: Next — Meridian Logistics. It's a different motion, long sales cycle. They asked about multi-region replication and audit logs; they also asked what kind of SSO we support.
[02:33] Ethan Brooks: We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and integrate with KMS for key management. Audit logs via Redwood Console, retention can be configured. For multi-region, we can route requests and set regional policies. There may be complexity if they need cross-account networking.
[02:48] Aisha Rao: Do you have examples of customers that used dedicated pools for multi-region?
[02:53] Ethan Brooks: Yes, we've had customers with dedicated zones and smart routing policies. I'll pull a short reference.

[03:00] Liam O'Neill: Great. Beacon Retail — more of a POC to test recommendation LLMs, lower risk, likely to start with hosted.

[03:10] Maya Chen: For prioritization, how do you feel about focusing immediate effort on Horizon (pilot) and Meridian (longer term), and spinning Beacon as a low-touch hosted POC?
[03:21] Priya Sharma: That aligns with our internal priorities. Horizon gives the quickest win and proof point for health vertical.

[03:30] Maya Chen: Cool. Let's deep dive Horizon — Ethan, can you walk through what we need to benchmark and typical artifacts?
[03:36] Ethan Brooks: Sure. For a pilot focused on latency and cost we usually need: sample prompts/loads, expected concurrency, average sequence length, example documents (de-identified), security requirements (SOC2, HIPAA), and success criteria. We then run a 2-week benchmark on a representative workload, measure p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and regression in quality.
[03:56] Aisha Rao: For Horizon, they can produce synthetic or de-identified data. Concurrency is roughly 80-120 rps during peaks, avg seq length 400 tokens.
[04:06] Ethan Brooks: That's good. 400 tokens is moderate — we can test quantized model variants to reduce cost while hitting latency. We'll probably test a 13B and an 70B quantized profile depending on quality.
[04:16] Liam O'Neill: Any chance of hitting 300ms p99 at 400 tokens with those models?
[04:21] Ethan Brooks: p99 under 300ms at 400 tokens is challenging for larger models; with batching strategies and dedicated GPUs it's plausible for smaller models or with caching for repeated prefixes. We need to set expectations: either we trade model size for latency, or accept slightly higher latency with better quality.
[04:36] Maya Chen: We'll prepare two benchmark scenarios: conservative (lower-latency smaller model + aggressive caching) and quality-first (larger model, expect higher latency).

[04:46] Priya Sharma: On contracting — Horizon asked about revenue share for co-sell. Starlake tends to expect standard 60/40 split for introduced accounts. Is that flexible?
[04:56] Maya Chen: We can be flexible on a case-by-case basis, especially for pilot-to-production conversions. We'll capture specifics and escalate to partnerships. Priya, maybe you and Liam can flag which deals you'd expect a larger split on.
[05:08] Priya Sharma: Yes, will do.

[05:12] Liam O'Neill: A couple of smaller items — partner portal access for Starlake reps, co-branded decks, and a suggested email intro template to share with Horizon.
[05:22] Maya Chen: We'll share partner portal invites and a co-sell kit. I can send a suggested email and one-pager today.

[05:28] Ethan Brooks: For the Horizon technical deep dive, ideally Aisha and I sync to align on artifacts before the benchmark. Can we plan a follow-up 60 min session?
[05:36] Aisha Rao: Yes, that works. Week of April 6 looks ok but we'll confirm.

[05:42] Maya Chen: Noted. I'll create a Doodle and propose April 6 or 7.

[06:00] [Minor crosstalk and clarification]
[06:18] Liam O'Neill: On objections we sometimes see — costs and data residency — Meridians will push hard on TCO and auditability. Do you have a pre-written security doc we can hand to their procurement?
[06:30] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share the SOC2 summary, our KMS/HSM options, SAML docs, and the security whitepaper. We'll also include an example security questionnaire response.
[06:42] Priya Sharma: Perfect. That will help move Meridian through procurement.

[06:48] Ethan Brooks: One note — sometimes transcription misreads product names, but internally we call the features Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private (VPC), Redwood Console, Redwood Optimize.

[07:00] Maya Chen: Ok quick review of the deals in the sheet: we flagged an estimated ACV (best guess) for Horizon at $450k ARR if pilot goes to prod, Meridian $1.2M but multi-year slow, Beacon $120k POC -> potential $350k ARR. Liam, are those ballparks accurate?
[07:18] Liam O'Neill: Yes those look about right.

[07:25] Priya Sharma: For Horizon, any legal constraints at pilot stage? They asked about data deletion windows and log retention.
[07:34] Maya Chen: At pilot stage we can configure retention and ensure data deletion; for production we'll contract specifics. We'll include standard options in the security docs.

[07:42] Aisha Rao: For the benchmark, do you have an estimate on how long to get results?
[07:46] Ethan Brooks: From kickoff to an initial benchmark report usually 10 business days if we have sample prompts and traffic profile. Could be quicker if the dataset is ready.
[07:55] Liam O'Neill: Ok we'll try to provide de-identified sample data by end of next week.

[08:02] Maya Chen: Great. A few administrative items
